subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw add a persisted per-job/per-heartbeat elevated authorization contract, and what trust/provenance model should replace provider-wide cron-event or heartbeat elevated allowlists?
rationale: The fix changes a core security boundary and persisted/configured scheduling semantics, so automation should not choose the trust model or migration policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design per-job elevated provenance
options.body: Add a narrow persisted authorization model for cron/heartbeat elevated runs, with owner-controlled creation/update rules and explicit upgrade behavior.

options.title: Fold into scheduling RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open but route the design through #71712 so agent-created schedules, provenance, quotas, and elevated authority are settled together.

options.title: Document current allowlist model
options.body: Reject the new elevated surface for now and document provider allowlists plus command cron as the supported operator-trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Design per-job elevated provenance
recommendation.body: Add a narrow persisted authorization model for cron/heartbeat elevated runs, with owner-controlled creation/update rules and explicit upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged cron caller-scope work is the nearest current-main implementation and provides the best starting point for the remaining cron authority decision.
